title: Addiction and Freedom
definition: Addiction and freedom addresses the bondage of enslaving desires, habits, substances, or behaviors and the freedom found through Christ, repentance, truth, discipleship, accountability, and the power of the Holy Spirit.
summary: Christ offers real freedom to people trapped in enslaving habits and destructive patterns.
christFocus: Jesus Christ breaks chains, forgives sinners, transforms hearts, and gives a new identity to those who trust Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Addiction is more than a physical struggle; it affects the heart, mind, body, relationships, and spiritual life. Scripture teaches that sin enslaves, but Christ sets people free. Freedom may involve repentance, accountability, wise counsel, support from other believers, and daily dependence upon God. Lasting freedom is found not merely in removing destructive behavior but in learning to walk with Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people trapped in addiction believe they are beyond hope or permanently defined by their past. The Gospel declares that no one is beyond God's grace. Understanding biblical freedom helps believers pursue recovery with hope rather than despair.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Be honest about areas of bondage. Bring them into the light before God and trusted believers. Build habits of prayer, Scripture, accountability, and fellowship. Remember that recovery is often a journey of daily faithfulness rather than a single moment of victory.
